abstract: BACKGROUND: Genistein is an isoflavonoid present in soybeans that exhibits anti-carcinogenic properties. The issue of genistein as a potential anti-cancer drug has been addressed in some papers, but comprehensive genomic analysis to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the effect elicited by genistein on cancer cells have not been performed on primary cancer cells, but rather on transformed cell lines. In the present study, we treated primary glioblastoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, hepatocellular carcinoma and human embryonic carcinoma cells (NCCIT) with mu-molar concentrations of genistein and assessed mitotic index, cell morphology, global gene expression, and specific cell-cycle regulating genes. We compared the expression profiles of NCCIT cells with that of the cancer cell lines in order to identify common genistein-dependent transcriptional changes and accompanying signaling cascades. METHODS: We treated primary cancer cells and NCCIT cells with 50 muM genistein for 48 h. Thereafter, we compared the mitotic index of treated versus untreated cells and investigated the protein expression of key regulatory self renewal factors as OCT4, SOX2 and NANOG. We then used gene expression arrays (Illumina) for genome-wide expression analysis and validated the results for genes of interest by means of Real-Time PCR. Functional annotations were then performed using the DAVID and KEGG online tools. RESULTS: We found that cancer cells treated with genistein undergo cell-cycle arrest at different checkpoints. This arrest was associated with a decrease in the mRNA levels of core regulatory genes, PBK, BUB1, and CDC20 as determined by microarray-analysis and verified by Real-Time PCR. In contrast, human NCCIT cells showed over-expression of GADD45 A and G (growth arrest- and DNA-damage-inducible proteins 45A and G), as well as down-regulation of OCT4, and NANOG protein. Furthermore, genistein induced the expression of apoptotic and anti-migratory proteins p53 and p38 in all cell lines. Genistein also up-regulated steady-state levels of both CYCLIN A and B. CONCLUSION: The results of the present study, together with the results of earlier studies show that genistein targets genes involved in the progression of the M-phase of the cell cycle. In this respect it is of particular interest that this conclusion cannot be drawn from comparison of the individual genes found differentially regulated in the datasets, but by the rather global view of the pathways influenced by genistein treatment.
abstract_ja:
背景：ゲニステインは大豆に含まれるイソフラボノイドで、抗発がん作用を示す。抗がん剤としての可能性は複数の研究で論じられてきたが、形質転換細胞株ではなく初代がん細胞を用いて、ゲニステインが細胞に及ぼす網羅的な分子機序を解析した研究はなかった。本研究では、初代膠芽腫、横紋筋肉腫、肝細胞癌、およびヒト胎児性癌細胞株(NCCIT)を50 μMのゲニステインで48時間処理した。有糸分裂指数、細胞形態、全遺伝子発現、細胞周期制御遺伝子を比較し、自己複製因子OCT4、SOX2、NANOGのタンパク質発現も調べた。遺伝子発現はIllumina社のアレイで網羅的に解析し、対象遺伝子はリアルタイムPCRで検証した。機能注釈はDAVIDおよびKEGGのオンラインツールを用いて行った。
結果：ゲニステイン処理により、がん細胞は異なるチェックポイントで細胞周期停止を起こした。この停止はPBK、BUB1、CDC20などの中核制御遺伝子のmRNA低下と関連していた。一方、NCCIT細胞ではGADD45AおよびGADD45Gの過剰発現と、OCT4およびNANOGタンパク質の減少がみられた。さらにゲニステインは全細胞株で、アポトーシスおよび抗遊走性のタンパク質であるp53とp38の発現を誘導した。また、サイクリンAおよびBの定常状態のレベルを上昇させた。
結論：本研究と先行研究の結果から、ゲニステインはM期の細胞周期進行に関わる遺伝子を標的とすることが示された。この結論は個々の差次的発現遺伝子の比較からは導けず、ゲニステインが影響する経路全体を俯瞰して初めて得られるものである。
